item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
013
ABNT20 KNHC 261734
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Gonzalo, located to the north of the Cabo Verde Islands, and
on Tropical Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of
the Azores.

Central Subtropical Atlantic:
A surface trough of low pressure located several hundred miles to
the southeast of Bermuda is currently producing an area of
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions
appear somewhat favorable for gradual development of this system as
it moves northward this weekend and then turns eastward by the early
to middle portion of next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

--------------------

DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 29.8 North, longitude 43.9 West. The
depression is moving toward the south near 2 mph (4 km/h), this 
motion is expected to continue for the next several days with a 
gradual increase in forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast over the next several days.!
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1009 mb (29.80 inches).

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 262038
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
The convection around Fay has been mostly stripped away by the wind
shear and the dry air in the environment. The latest TAFB Dvorak
fix was T2.0/30 kt and the objective intensity estimate is in the
range of 29-39 kt. Given that there has been little change in the 
intensity estimates, the initial intensity has been held at 30 kt 
for this advisory.
 
The cyclone is now slowly moving towards the south, at 180/2 kt. Fay 
is expected to continue to move southward into the southern flank of 
the subtropical Atlantic high. By early next week, the depression 
should turn westward due to the large-scale easterly flow, but there 
is still some uncertainty in the timing of this turn. The current 
NHC forecast track is similar to the previous one with some small 
adjustments based on the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
 
The intensity forecast continues to have a high level of 
uncertainty as Fay is still over favorably warm sea-surface 
temperatures. However, vertical wind shear and dry mid-level air 
continue to hinder the depression and preventing a more organized 
structure from developing. Both the GFS and ECMWF SHIPS 
statistical analysis have mid-level relative humidity less than 40 
percent for the next several days. Convection is likely to continue 
to pulse up and down, but the current NHC intensity forecast 
follows the trend of the previous one showing little change in 
strength with only minor changes made. This forecast continues to 
maintain Fay as a tropical depression until it become post-tropical 
and dissipates by the middle of next week.

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Gonzalo Public Advisory Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
885 
WTNT32 KNHC 262037
TCPAT2
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Gonzalo Advisory Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
800 PM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
...GONZALO NO LONGER A TROPICAL CYCLONE...
...THIS IS THE FINAL ADVISORY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM CVT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.3N 23.3W
ABOUT 180 MI...290 KM N OF SAL CABO VERDE
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 345 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM CVT (2100 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone 
Gonzalo was located near latitude 19.3 North, longitude 23.3 West. 
The post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the north-northwest near 
7 mph (11 km/h) and this general motion is forecast to continue 
through the weekend, with a slow down and turn to the west-northwest 
expected by early next week.

Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Additional weakening is forecast, and the post-tropical cyclone is 
expected to dissipate over eastern Subtropical Atlantic by the 
early to mid portion of next week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Gonzalo are expected to affect portions
of the Cabo Verde Islands this evening before diminishing Sunday.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. Additional information on this system can be 
found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, 
under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and online at 
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Gonzalo Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTNT42 KNHC 262038
TCDAT2
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Gonzalo Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
800 PM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026

The bulk of the convective activity associated with Gonzalo has 
become even further separated from its center this afternoon. This 
increased separation is due to strong southwesterly vertical wind 
shear, diagnosed at nearly 50 kt this afternoon by UW-CIMSS. In 
addition, water vapor imagery shows very dry air infiltrating the 
low-level circulation, limiting convective redevelopment. Given that 
the nearest convection is now more than 100 n mi away from the 
center, lacks sufficient organization, and that these very 
unfavorable conditions are likely to persist, Gonzalo is being 
declared a post-tropical cyclone in this advisory. The maximum 
sustained winds remain 35 kt, assuming some higher winds exist in 
the convection displaced well northeast of the center. The 
post-tropical cyclone is still moving off to the north-northeast at 
045 degrees at 6 kt. Downshear convection may still attempt to tug 
the center more northward over the next 12-24 h. However, as this 
activity diminishes, a shallow low-level ridge should steer the 
remnant low more west-northwest during the early portion of next 
week before dissipation.

This is the final NHC advisory on Gonzalo. Additional information 
on this system can be found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the 
National Weather Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header 
FZNT01 KWBC, and online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php
